rows.title: Mitte
rows.summary: Historic centre of Berlin: highest expat density, premium rents, outstanding transit and culture.
rows.body: Berlin Mitte is the governmental, cultural, and commercial heart of the city, home to the Brandenburg Gate, Museumsinsel (UNESCO World Heritage), Alexanderplatz, and the Reichstag. With 37% foreign residents it is the most internationally diverse district in Berlin — English is spoken virtually everywhere in shops, cafés, and offices. Major tech companies, startups, embassies, and Bundestag offices are all concentrated here. Rental prices are Berlin's highest at roughly €18–23/m², translating to approximately €1,800–3,500/month for a 2–3 bedroom apartment. Excellent public transport with U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram, and bus connections. The 210-hectare Tiergarten park anchors the western side. International schools nearby include Berlin Metropolitan School, Berlin Cosmopolitan School, Phorms Berlin Mitte, and the Lycée Français. Better suited to young professionals and corporate expats than families seeking larger homes; limited family-sized housing stock at mid-range prices.

rows.title: Prenzlauer Berg
rows.summary: Berlin's top family neighbourhood: charming altbau streets, café culture, parks, and strong expat community.
rows.body: Prenzlauer Berg (part of Pankow Bezirk) is consistently rated Berlin's favourite neighbourhood for young families and creative professionals. Beautifully restored pre-war altbau apartment buildings line wide avenues, while Helmholtzplatz, Kollwitzplatz, and Volkspark Prenzlauer Berg provide ample green space. The district has one of the highest concentrations of playgrounds per capita in Germany. Rents are among Berlin's highest outside Mitte at €15–22/m², with 2–3BR apartments running €1,500–2,800/month. Excellent U2 and tram connections link the area to central Berlin in 10–15 minutes. The neighbourhood is very stroller- and child-friendly with a dense network of Kitas, bilingual kindergartens, and proximity to Phorms Berlin Prenzlauer Berg and Berlin Bilingual School. High English proficiency among residents; large French, Scandinavian, and American expat communities. The thriving café and restaurant scene on Kastanienallee and Pappelallee adds to the neighbourhood's appeal.

rows.title: Charlottenburg
rows.summary: Traditional West Berlin: established expat community, grand boulevards, luxury shopping, and strong corporate presence.
rows.body: Charlottenburg (part of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf Bezirk) is the traditional heart of West Berlin and home to the grandest residential streets in the city. Kurfürstendamm (Ku'damm) provides world-class shopping, while Schloss Charlottenburg and the Tiergarten are within easy reach. The district hosts a disproportionately large share of Berlin's diplomatic community, multinational corporate offices, and long-established expat families. Approximately 23% of residents are foreign nationals. Rents run €16–20/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,600–3,000/month. Excellent U-Bahn (U2, U7) and S-Bahn connections. Berlin British School is located here (Dickensweg 17–19). Good family infrastructure with established schools and spacious altbau apartments. Quieter and more traditional in character than eastern neighbourhoods; particularly attractive to senior executives and diplomatic families who value discretion and established services.

rows.title: Schöneberg
rows.summary: Diverse, central, and well-connected: popular with LGBTQ+ community, families, and value-conscious expats.
rows.body: Schöneberg (part of Tempelhof-Schöneberg Bezirk) offers a lively, diverse neighbourhood that balances central access with more affordable rents than Mitte or Prenzlauer Berg. The Akazienstraße area around Goltzstraße is a hub of independent cafés, delis, and family-friendly restaurants. Schöneberg is internationally known as Berlin's LGBTQ+ heartland, centred on Motzstraße and Nollendorfplatz, creating a notably open and welcoming social atmosphere. Winterfeldtplatz hosts one of Berlin's best weekly markets (Wednesday and Saturday). Rents average €13–15/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,300–2,200/month. Good U-Bahn connections (U1, U2, U3, U4, U7) and proximity to the Gleisdreieck park. Solid family infrastructure with parks and Kitas. Particularly popular with expats seeking a central, walkable neighbourhood at mid-range prices. The Bundesallee corridor is increasingly popular with professionals priced out of Mitte.

rows.title: Kreuzberg
rows.summary: Creative, multicultural, and energetic: Berlin's cultural engine with a thriving tech and arts scene.
rows.body: Kreuzberg (part of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg Bezirk) is one of Berlin's most internationally diverse and creatively vibrant areas. The district divides into two distinct halves: the anarchic, alternative SO36 zone around Oranienstraße and Görlitzer Park, and the more gentrified Bergmannkiez with charming cafés, Viktoriapark, and a strong young professional community. Germany's largest Turkish community is centred here, providing excellent food markets including the famous Turkish Market on Maybachufer (Tuesday and Friday). Rents range from €17–22/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,400–2,500/month. Excellent U-Bahn (U1, U8) and bus connections. Strong English-speaking expat community, particularly from tech, creative, and startup sectors. The Görlitzer Park area sees some drug-related activity but residential streets are safe. Growing family presence in Bergmannkiez. Proximity to Tempodrom and Anhalter Bahnhof makes central Berlin very accessible.

rows.title: Friedrichshain
rows.summary: Young, vibrant East Berlin: nightlife, East Side Gallery, improving family scene, and mid-range rents.
rows.body: Friedrichshain is Berlin's densest district and a magnet for young European, Australian, American, and Latin American expats drawn by its nightlife, creative energy, and relative affordability. The East Side Gallery (the longest remaining section of the Berlin Wall) runs along the Spree, flanked by new residential and cultural developments. The RAW-Gelände entertainment complex, Berghain, and dozens of clubs make this the global capital of electronic music culture. Rents average €17–20/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,300–2,200/month. Boxhagener Platz hosts a popular weekend flea market and farmers market. Excellent S-Bahn (Warschauer Straße) and U5 connections. The neighbourhood is increasingly family-friendly in the quieter streets north of Karl-Marx-Allee. Simon-Dach-Straße is the social hub with restaurants and bars. Proximity to Volkspark Friedrichshain provides green space for families.

rows.title: Wilmersdorf
rows.summary: Leafy, residential West Berlin: safe, family-friendly, home to embassies and corporate expats.
rows.body: Wilmersdorf (part of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf Bezirk) is one of Berlin's safest and most prestigious residential districts, consistently ranked among the lowest crime areas in the city. Wide, tree-lined streets, detached villas, and well-maintained altbau blocks characterise the neighbourhood. The Kudamm shopping boulevard is easily accessible, and the Grunewald forest and Schlachtensee lake are within cycling distance. A high concentration of foreign embassies, UN agencies, and multinational company offices creates a strong diplomatic and international professional community. Nelson Mandela School (a bilingual public IB school) is located in Wilmersdorf. Rents are mid-to-premium at €16–19/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,500–2,800/month. Good U-Bahn (U3, U7, U9) connections. Particularly attractive to families with school-age children and professionals seeking a quieter, more residential lifestyle while maintaining easy city access.

rows.title: Steglitz-Zehlendorf
rows.summary: Suburban, green, and family-oriented: excellent schools, lakes, and proximity to international school corridor.
rows.body: Steglitz-Zehlendorf is Berlin's most suburban Bezirk, stretching southwest from the city centre through leafy residential areas to the Grunewald forest and a string of scenic lakes (Wannsee, Schlachtensee, Krumme Lanke). It is one of Berlin's safest districts with the lowest residential crime rates. The area is well known as home to several top international and bilingual schools, including JFK School (Zehlendorf), Berlin International School (Dahlem), and Berlin Brandenburg International School just across the district border in Kleinmachnow. Predominantly single-family homes and large apartments make this ideal for families. Rents average €13–17/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,400–2,500/month. Good S-Bahn connections (S1, S3, S7) and U-Bahn (U3). English is widely spoken. Particularly favoured by families moving to Berlin for 2–5 year postings who prioritise school proximity and a quieter suburban lifestyle.

rows.title: Tempelhof-Schöneberg
rows.summary: Well-connected central-south Berlin: residential, good transit, mid-range prices, and Tempelhofer Feld.
rows.body: Tempelhof-Schöneberg combines the lively urban character of Schöneberg with the more residential Tempelhof area in the south. The former Tempelhof Airport (Tempelhofer Feld) is now Europe's largest urban park, a 386-hectare open space used for cycling, barbecues, kite-flying, and community events — a major quality-of-life advantage for residents. The district has a 23% foreign resident share with a notably LGBTQ+ welcoming atmosphere. Rents average €13–15/m² with 2–3BR apartments at €1,200–2,100/month — among the better value central options. Excellent U-Bahn connectivity (U4, U6, U7) and good S-Bahn access. The Bergmannstraße area in northern Tempelhof is particularly popular with families and young couples. Mid-range restaurants, independent shops, and a growing café scene make the area increasingly attractive to expat families seeking central access without Mitte prices.

rows.title: Pankow
rows.summary: North Berlin's family hub: Berlin's most populous district with excellent parks, schools, and diverse sub-neighbourhoods.
rows.body: Pankow is Berlin's largest and most populous Bezirk (427,000 residents), encompassing several distinct and popular sub-neighbourhoods including Prenzlauer Berg, Weißensee, and Pankow Mitte. The outer Pankow areas beyond Prenzlauer Berg offer noticeably more affordable rents — €12–18/m² — while maintaining the family-friendly character and green space that makes the wider district so popular. Bürgerpark Pankow and Weißensee lake provide excellent outdoor facilities. The district is home to Platanus School (bilingual German-English), strong Kita provision, and good state school options. S-Bahn (S8, S9, S2, S85) and tram networks link the area to central Berlin. Particularly attractive to families who want the Prenzlauer Berg lifestyle at more accessible price points. The 21% foreign resident share means an active international community. Pankow is one of the city's fastest-growing residential areas due to ongoing urban development north of the centre.

rows.title: Spandau
rows.summary: Western Berlin: quieter, spacious, and budget-friendly — ideal for families seeking more room at lower cost.
rows.body: Spandau is Berlin's westernmost and one of its most affordable districts, with rents among the lowest in the city at approximately €12/m², making it a strong option for families needing larger homes on tighter budgets. The historic Altstadt Spandau, one of the best-preserved medieval old towns in eastern Germany, gives the area a distinct character different from inner Berlin. The Havel River and Spandauer Forst provide extensive outdoor recreation, including boating, cycling, and walking. The district has approximately 247,000 residents with around 20% foreign nationals. U7 provides a direct connection to central Berlin, though journey times of 30–40 minutes make this a more committed commute. Particularly attractive to families working in western Berlin or at companies near the Siemensstadt industrial/tech campus. English is less widely spoken than in central districts. Good local amenities including Arcaden shopping centre. Best suited to families who prioritise space and affordability over central access.

rows.title: Treptow-Köpenick
rows.summary: East Berlin's nature retreat: lakes, forests, family-friendly living, and affordable rents near research hubs.
rows.body: Treptow-Köpenick is Berlin's largest Bezirk by area, covering the southeastern portion of the city and encompassing the Müggelsee (Berlin's largest lake), the Köpenick Altstadt, and extensive Forst Köpenick woodland. The district offers an exceptional quality of outdoor life: sailing, kayaking, cycling, and swimming are accessible year-round. Rents are among the most affordable for a relatively central location at €12–14/m², with 2–3BR apartments at €1,100–1,800/month. The Adlershof technology and science park (one of Germany's largest technology parks, home to Humboldt University's natural science faculties) employs many international researchers and academics. S-Bahn (S3, S8, S9) provides connections to central Berlin in 25–40 minutes. The 16% foreign resident share is lower than central districts, but a strong international academic community exists. Particularly well-suited to researchers, academics, and families seeking a quieter, nature-oriented lifestyle at affordable prices.

rows.title: Neukölln
rows.summary: Berlin's most rapidly gentrifying district: budget-friendly, highly diverse, with a booming creative scene.
rows.body: Neukölln has transformed dramatically over the past decade from one of Berlin's most disadvantaged areas to a thriving creative and cultural hub. The Reuterkiez (around Weserstraße and Reuterkiez) and Rixdorf are now among the most sought-after affordable neighbourhoods, popular with artists, musicians, digital nomads, and budget-conscious young professionals. The district has a 28% foreign resident share, one of the highest in Berlin, and extraordinary cultural diversity including large Arab, Turkish, and Southeast European communities. Rents of €12–16/m² make it significantly more affordable than comparable central districts, with 2–3BR apartments at €1,100–1,800/month. Good U-Bahn (U7, U8) connectivity. Particularly popular with those priced out of Kreuzberg and Prenzlauer Berg. The area around Hermannplatz is less family-friendly but improving; the southern Britz area is notably quieter and more residential. Proximity to the Tempelhof airfield park is a major draw.

rows.title: Berlin Brandenburg International School (BBIS)
rows.summary: Leading IB day and boarding school for international families, 20 minutes from central Berlin.
rows.body: Berlin Brandenburg International School is a fully authorised IB World School offering all three IB programmes: Primary Years Programme (PYP, Early Education through Grade 5), Middle Years Programme (MYP, Grades 6–10), and Diploma Programme (DP, Grades 11–12), plus IB Career-related Programme. Instruction is in English. The school serves students from Early Education (age 3) through to Grade 12 (age 18) and has over 700 students from 35+ nationalities. Located on a spacious campus in Kleinmachnow (Schopfheimer Allee 10, 14532 Kleinmachnow), approximately 20 minutes by car or S-Bahn from central Berlin. The school also offers a boarding programme for Years 9–12. Annual tuition for 2025/26 ranges approximately €18,000–25,000 depending on year group. Admissions contact: +49 33203 80360. Strong IBDP results and a well-established expat community. Particularly attractive to families in Steglitz-Zehlendorf and southwestern Berlin.

rows.title: John F. Kennedy School Berlin (JFKS)
rows.summary: Tuition-free German-American bilingual public school in Zehlendorf with 1,600+ students from Grade EC to 12.
rows.body: John F. Kennedy School is a unique public bilingual, bicultural German-American school founded in 1960, located in Zehlendorf (Teltower Damm 87–93, 14167 Berlin). The school serves 1,600+ students from Entrance Class (age 5) through Grade 12 (age 18). All instruction is bilingual in German and English across the full curriculum. As a tuition-free public state school (Gesamtschule), it represents exceptional value but competition for places is intense; US Embassy families receive priority. Annual application deadlines are January 31 (Entrance Class) and March 31 (Elementary and High School). The High School offers both a German Abitur and an American High School Diploma. Students from non-English and non-German speaking backgrounds face challenges with the immersive bilingual approach. Very strong alumni community and excellent college placement. Conveniently located in southwestern Berlin near the international school corridor, accessible by S1 S-Bahn and bus.
rows.price_range_text: Tuition-free public school (exam fees may apply)

rows.title: Berlin Metropolitan School (BMS)
rows.summary: Oldest and largest international school in central Berlin, offering IB and Cambridge programmes from ELC to Grade 12.
rows.body: Berlin Metropolitan School is the oldest international school in central Berlin and one of four international schools within the city centre. Located at Linienstraße 122, 10115 Berlin (Mitte), the school serves students from Early Learning Centre (age 3) through Secondary School (Grade 12, age 18). The curriculum includes IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), Cambridge IGCSE, and IB Diploma Programme (DP). Fees are income-based: monthly tuition ranges from approximately €210 to €1,340 (equivalent to roughly €2,520–€16,080/year), with a one-time €1,100 admission fee. The income-based model makes BMS more accessible than fixed-fee international schools. Instruction is in English with German as a second language. The school has 50+ nationalities enrolled. Strong pastoral care, house system, and Model United Nations programme. Particularly convenient for families living in Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, and Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg.

rows.title: Phorms Berlin Mitte
rows.summary: Bilingual German-English private school in Mitte with full immersion from nursery to Abitur for ages 2–18.
rows.body: Phorms Berlin Mitte (Ackerstraße 76, 13355 Berlin) is a bilingual German-English private school offering continuous education from nursery (age 2) through to Abitur/secondary graduation (age 18), with approximately 950 students enrolled. The Phorms approach focuses on full language immersion, with heavy English concentration in early years and increasing German integration as students progress through secondary school. The curriculum includes Cambridge International Primary Programme, Mittlere Schulabschluss (MSA), Abitur, and USA Advanced Placement (AP). Monthly school fees are income-dependent, ranging from €118 to €519/month for primary and €118 to €698/month for secondary, making annual tuition approximately €1,416–€8,376. This income-based fee structure makes Phorms more financially accessible than most international schools. English and German are both languages of instruction throughout. A second Phorms campus is located in Prenzlauer Berg (Storkower Straße), and a third in Zehlendorf (Berlin-Süd, Harry-S.-Truman-Allee 3, 14167 Berlin). Very popular with mixed German-international families.

rows.title: Berlin International School (B.I.S.)
rows.summary: IB World School in Dahlem for Grades 1–12, with English and German instruction and 70+ nationalities.
rows.body: Berlin International School (Lentzeallee 8/14, 14195 Berlin, Dahlem) is a state-recognised IB World School serving students from Grade 1 (age 6) through Grade 12 (age 18). The school has approximately 820 students from over 70 nationalities. Instruction is in English and German throughout. The curriculum follows IB PYP (Grades 1–5), IB MYP (Grades 6–10 leading to Berlin MSA), and IB Diploma Programme (Grades 11–12). The school is accredited by the Council of International Schools (CIS) and Middle States Association (MSA-CESS). Annual tuition for 2025/26: Grades 1–6 €12,300/year (€1,025/month); Grades 7–10 €13,560/year (€1,130/month); Grades 11–12 €18,240/year (€1,520/month). One-time admission fee: €800. Located in the prestigious Dahlem academic quarter of Steglitz-Zehlendorf, near the Free University of Berlin. Strong pastoral care, arts, and sports programme. Very well-suited to corporate expat families on postings.

rows.title: Lycée Français de Berlin
rows.summary: French-curriculum school in Tiergarten offering French Baccalaureate for ages 12–18 with French, German and English.
rows.body: The Lycée Français de Berlin (Derfflingerstraße 7, 10785 Berlin, Tiergarten/Mitte) is a publicly funded French-curriculum school operated within the framework of the French Agency for Teaching Abroad (AEFE). The school primarily serves the secondary level (Grades 5–12 / ages 11–18), preparing students for the French Baccalaureate. Instruction is primarily in French, with strong German and English language components; Latin is introduced from Grade 5 (5ème) and Ancient Greek from Grade 4. The school emphasises French-German cultural friendship and multilingualism. As a publicly funded institution, tuition is low to moderate: annual fees range approximately €3,000–€5,500/year depending on grade level and family income, with some income-based fee reductions. Approximately 558 pupils enrolled. Strongly favoured by French diplomatic and expatriate families, as well as Francophile international families. Well located near Potsdamer Platz with good transport links.

rows.title: Berlin British School (BBS)
rows.summary: IB World School in Charlottenburg offering British-curriculum education with IGCSE and IB Diploma for ages 3–18.
rows.body: Berlin British School (Dickensweg 17–19, 14055 Berlin, Charlottenburg) is a private English-medium IB World School serving students from Early Years/Kita (age 3) through Secondary School (age 18). The school runs IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), English National Curriculum, IGCSE, and IB Diploma Programme across its monolingual and bilingual streams. Annual school fees for 2026/27 range from approximately €13,100 (lower primary) to €22,500 (upper secondary/IBDP), with additional charges for after-school care, lunch, and music lessons. A small annual development fee (approximately 2% of tuition) applies. Sibling discounts of approximately 2.5% are offered. The school is a not-for-profit limited company governed by the Berlin British School e.V. association. Very strong reputation for British educational standards in Berlin. Well-located in Charlottenburg near Olympiastadion, accessible by U2 and S-Bahn. Particularly popular with British families and those seeking a UK university preparation pathway.

rows.title: Berlin Cosmopolitan School
rows.summary: IB World School in central Mitte offering bilingual English-German education from nursery to IB Diploma.
rows.body: Berlin Cosmopolitan School is a private bilingual English-German IB World School located in one of the most desirable streets in central Berlin Mitte. The school offers continuous education from Early Years (Nursery/Kindergarten) through Secondary School (Grade 12), with over 700 students enrolled. The curriculum includes IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), Berlin Rahmenlehrplan (MSA), Bilingual Abitur, and IB Diploma Programme (DP). All students wear a school uniform. The school follows an immersive bilingual approach with both English and German as languages of instruction throughout. The central Mitte location makes it exceptionally convenient for families living in Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, and Friedrichshain. Annual tuition fees range approximately €12,000–€19,000 depending on year group. The school has strong IB results and an active international parent community. Particularly attractive to families seeking a full German-English bilingual track from early childhood through secondary graduation.

rows.title: Orchard / River Valley
rows.summary: Prime central district; luxury expat housing, malls, embassies.
rows.body: The Orchard / River Valley area is Singapore's most prestigious residential zone for expatriates. Lined with luxury condos, international schools nearby, shopping malls, and embassies. River Valley Road is particularly popular for families seeking easy access to Orchard Road's amenities. Robertson Quay and Mohammed Sultan Road attract singles and young couples for nightlife along the Singapore River. Rents are among Singapore's highest. Excellent MRT access (Somerset, Orchard, Great World stations). The American Club and Tanglin Club are nearby. Popular with senior corporate executives, diplomats, and finance professionals.

rows.title: Holland Village / Dempsey
rows.summary: Classic expat enclave with bohemian vibe, restaurants, boutiques, and easy access to nature.
rows.body: Holland Village ('Holland V') is one of Singapore's most enduring expat favourites. It offers a bohemian atmosphere with a rich mix of restaurants, bars, independent boutiques, and Holland Village Shopping Centre. Neighbouring Dempsey Hill provides upscale dining, furniture stores, and weekend family activities in a colonial heritage setting. Sixth Avenue connects Holland V to Bukit Timah, with family houses featuring gardens, cluster homes, and attractive condominiums. Excellent preschools and international schools nearby (Tanglin Trust, Canadian International School). Circle and Downtown MRT lines provide good connectivity. Popular with Western expats from Europe, Australia, and North America.

rows.title: Buona Vista / one-north
rows.summary: Singapore's tech and biotech innovation hub; research institutes, universities, professionals.
rows.body: The Buona Vista / one-north precinct is Singapore's dedicated science and technology corridor. Home to Biopolis (biomedical research), Fusionopolis (info-communications and media), and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR). The National University of Singapore (NUS) is immediately adjacent. The area attracts researchers, tech professionals, and academics. Housing ranges from condos in the surrounding Queenstown and Clementi areas to expat apartments. West Coast and Pasir Panjang are up-and-coming nearby areas. MRT access via Buona Vista, one-north, and Commonwealth stations. More affordable than the traditional expat enclaves with growing amenities.

rows.title: Novena / Newton
rows.summary: Central medical cluster; modern condos, excellent MRT access, popular with younger expats.
rows.body: Novena and Newton sit just north of Orchard, offering a mix of high-rise condominiums and landed houses. Novena is home to Singapore's private medical cluster including Tan Tock Seng Hospital and numerous specialist clinics — popular with healthcare professionals and expats seeking excellent medical access. The famous Newton Food Centre is one of Singapore's oldest hawker centres. Balestier Road nearby has a unique heritage shophouse character. Multiple MRT lines (Novena and Newton stations) provide fast access to the CBD and Orchard. More affordable than Orchard while maintaining excellent central connectivity. Popular with younger expat couples and professionals.

rows.title: East Coast / Katong
rows.summary: Beach-adjacent Peranakan heritage district; popular with expat families near international schools.
rows.body: The East Coast and Katong area (Districts 15/16) blends Peranakan cultural heritage with a relaxed coastal lifestyle. East Coast Park provides beachfront cycling, seafood dining, and outdoor recreation minutes from home. Katong's colourful shophouses house independent cafes, boutiques, and Nyonya restaurants. The area has a strong expat family community, with good proximity to international schools including UWCSEA East Campus (Tampines), Chatsworth, and various preschools. Siglap and Marine Parade sub-districts offer quiet residential streets. The Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) has improved access to the city centre and north. Rents are more moderate than the core western expat areas.

rows.title: Tanjong Pagar / CBD
rows.summary: Singapore's business district; walkable, vibrant F&B scene, popular with young professionals.
rows.body: Tanjong Pagar and the broader Central Business District (CBD) area offer a dynamic urban lifestyle for professionals who work in the financial district. Tanjong Pagar Road and Duxton Hill are celebrated for their dense restaurant, bar, and café scene in restored shophouses. The Pinnacle@Duxton is an iconic HDB complex while Telok Ayer and Club Street attract creative and media industry workers. Tiong Bahru, immediately adjacent, is a trendy Art Deco heritage neighbourhood with excellent markets, bakeries, and an artsy café culture. The area suits singles and DINK (dual income no kids) expats. Excellent MRT connectivity (Tanjong Pagar, Outram Park, Telok Ayer stations).

rows.title: Sentosa Cove
rows.summary: Ultra-premium island enclave; waterfront villas, marina berths, exclusive gated community.
rows.body: Sentosa Cove is Singapore's only waterfront residential precinct where foreigners are permitted to buy landed property. This ultra-exclusive gated community on Sentosa Island offers detached bungalows, semi-detached homes, and luxury condominiums with private marina berths. Residents enjoy resort-style living with world-class amenities including W Hotel, One°15 Marina Club, and proximity to Resorts World Sentosa. The area is home primarily to ultra-high-net-worth individuals, top executives, and the super-wealthy expat community. Access is via Sentosa Gateway bridge or ferry. Rents can reach SGD 30,000-65,000/month for bungalows with marina views. Limited public transport but harbour front MRT is nearby.

rows.title: Woodlands / Admiralty
rows.summary: North Singapore near Malaysian border; family-friendly, Singapore American School catchment area.
rows.body: Woodlands and Admiralty in north Singapore (Districts 25/27) are particularly popular with American and other Western expat families due to the Singapore American School (SAS) being located here. The proximity to the Causeway and Malaysia border makes frequent cross-border trips easy. The area has a more suburban feel with larger condos and landed housing options at more affordable prices than the central districts. Admiralty Park and Woodlands Waterfront offer good recreational amenities. The Thomson-East Coast MRT Line provides direct connection to the city centre. The area has grown significantly with newer malls like Causeway Point and Woodlands Civic Centre.

rows.title: Bukit Timah
rows.summary: Leafy, family-oriented enclave near nature reserve and top international schools.
rows.body: Bukit Timah is among Singapore's most desirable residential districts for expat families. The area backs onto Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, Singapore's primary rainforest patch, making it ideal for nature lovers. Sixth Avenue connects Bukit Timah to Holland Village, lined with large family houses with gardens, cluster homes, and attractive condominiums. Key advantages include proximity to numerous international schools (Tanglin Trust School, Canadian International School, German European School) and the renowned Raffles Girls' and Henry Park Primary schools. King Albert Park and Beauty World MRT stations on the Downtown Line provide connectivity. Good Golf clubs and recreational facilities nearby.

rows.title: Tampines / Simei
rows.summary: East Singapore HDB heartland; budget-friendly for expats, growing amenities and MRT access.
rows.body: Tampines and Simei (District 18) represent Singapore's classic 'heartland' HDB new town in the east, offering significantly more affordable housing options for budget-conscious expats. Tampines has one of Singapore's largest suburban malls (Tampines Mall, Century Square, Tampines 1) and excellent recreational facilities. The East-West and Downtown MRT lines provide direct access to the CBD. UWCSEA East Campus is located in Tampines, making it particularly relevant for families with children at that school. The area is popular with expats from Malaysia and Indonesia who prefer a more local Singapore residential experience. Large green spaces including Bedok Reservoir and Tampines Eco Green are nearby.

rows.title: Jurong East
rows.summary: Western Singapore's commercial hub; newer developments, growing expat community, good value.
rows.body: Jurong East (District 22) is Singapore's major western hub and has been designated as a future 'second CBD.' The area has undergone significant transformation with Jurong Lake District development plans, JEM and Westgate malls, and the International Business Park. The Canadian International School's Lakeside campus is located in Jurong West, making this area popular with families attending that school. The Australian International School is also accessible from this area. Jurong Lake Gardens provides excellent recreational space. The East-West MRT Line connects Jurong East to the city centre in about 30-35 minutes. Housing is generally newer and more affordable than traditional expat enclaves.

rows.title: Punggol
rows.summary: New waterfront eco-town; modern infrastructure, young families, budget-friendly north-east Singapore.
rows.body: Punggol (District 19) is Singapore's newest, purpose-built eco-town developed as a 21st-century waterfront community. The Punggol Waterway and Coney Island Park offer scenic living with excellent jogging and cycling paths. The town has a young demographic profile and modern infrastructure, making it attractive for younger expat families seeking space and value. The Punggol Digital District is bringing tech employment to the area. Punggol LRT and MRT (north-east line) connect to the rest of Singapore, though commute times to the CBD are approximately 45-60 minutes. Increasing numbers of expats are choosing Punggol for its community feel, newer housing stock, and significantly lower rents compared to traditional central areas.

rows.title: Singapore American School (SAS)
rows.summary: Largest American curriculum international school in Singapore, pre-K to Grade 12.
rows.body: Singapore American School (SAS) is a non-profit, independent, co-educational day school founded in 1956. Located in Woodlands in north Singapore at 40 Woodlands Street 41. One of the largest international schools in Asia with approximately 4,000 students across pre-K through Grade 12. SAS follows an American curriculum and is accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC). The school is undergoing a major campus transformation ('SAS Reimagined'). Strong sports programmes as a member of IASAS. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 32,500 for elementary to SGD 44,000+ for high school, plus facility and other fees totalling SGD 45,000-55,000+ per year for grades 9-12. Popular with American corporate expats and families on packages.

rows.title: United World College South East Asia (UWCSEA)
rows.summary: Premier IB school with two campuses; Dover (central) and East (Tampines), K1 to Grade 12.
rows.body: UWCSEA is widely regarded as one of Singapore's top international schools and among the best IB schools in Asia. The school operates two campuses: Dover Campus at 1207 Dover Road (opened 1971, near NUS) and East Campus at 1 Tampines Street 73. Both offer the full IB curriculum from kindergarten through IB Diploma. Total enrolment across both campuses is approximately 6,000 students from over 100 nationalities. UWCSEA is known for its holistic education model emphasising academic, activity, service, and outdoor education. Annual tuition starts at approximately SGD 39,000 rising to SGD 47,000+ for IB Diploma years; total first-year costs (including one-time fees) can reach SGD 54,000+. Highly competitive admissions.

rows.title: Canadian International School (CIS)
rows.summary: Well-established IB school at Lakeside campus; ages 2-18, strong Canadian-international community.
rows.body: Canadian International School (CIS) is a well-established IB World School located at 7 Jurong West Street 41 (Lakeside Campus) in western Singapore. Founded in 1990, CIS serves students aged 2 to 18 and offers the full IB programme from Primary Years Programme (PYP) through IB Diploma. The school has a strong arts, sports, and extracurricular programme. With over 400 co-curricular offerings, it has one of the broadest activity programmes in Singapore. Annual fees range from approximately SGD 20,780 for Early Childhood up to SGD 39,940+ for secondary and IB Diploma levels. The school draws students from over 60 nationalities with a particularly strong Canadian, British, and Australian community.

rows.title: Australian International School (AIS)
rows.summary: Offers Australian curriculum (HSC) and IB; single campus in Lorong Chuan, ages 2 months to 18.
rows.body: Australian International School (AIS) is located at 1 Lorong Chuan, Singapore (near Lorong Chuan MRT station on the Circle Line). AIS is unique in Singapore for offering both the Australian HASS/HSC curriculum and the International Baccalaureate (IB), making it the school of choice for Australian families and those who may return to Australia. It serves students from 2 months (infant care) through Year 12. Facilities include a pool, sports fields, and performing arts centre. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 31,356 for Prep-Year 5 rising to SGD 51,600 for Years 10-12, plus one-time enrolment fees. Over $2.67 million in scholarships is offered annually.

rows.title: Tanglin Trust School
rows.summary: Top British-curriculum international school; Portsdown Road, ages 3-18, not-for-profit.
rows.body: Tanglin Trust School is one of Singapore's most prestigious and longest-established international schools, founded in 1925. Located on Portsdown Road (off Holland Road) in central Singapore. As a not-for-profit school, all tuition fees are reinvested directly into the school. Offers a British-based curriculum from Infant School through to A-Levels and IB Diploma. Consistently ranked as one of the top British international schools in Asia. Annual fees for 2026/27 are approximately SGD 34,770 per trimester (tuition component) with additional enrolment fees of SGD 4,500 and capital levy of SGD 4,500 for new students. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 38,000 (primary) to SGD 55,000+ (sixth form). Accredited by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).

rows.title: Dover Court International School (DCIS)
rows.summary: Nord Anglia school on Dover Road; British and IB curricula, ages 3-18.
rows.body: Dover Court International School (DCIS) is part of the Nord Anglia Education group and is located on Dover Road in central Singapore. DCIS offers adapted British and IB curricula across both a primary and secondary school, serving students from ages 3 to 18. The school has approximately 2,000 students from over 50 nationalities. Six core educational pillars including wellbeing, arts, and sport frame the curriculum. As part of Nord Anglia, students benefit from global collaborations with Juilliard and MIT. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 29,178 in Early Years to SGD 45,609 in Sixth Form. DCIS is positioned as a mid-premium option, meaningfully more affordable than UWCSEA or Tanglin Trust. A new campus development is planned.

rows.title: ISS International School
rows.summary: Singapore's oldest IB Continuum school; Preston Road location, arts-rich holistic education.
rows.body: ISS International School, established in 1981, is one of Singapore's oldest and most well-established international schools. The main campus is at 21 Preston Road (Telok Blangah area), nestled among the treetops of Telok Blangah Hill National Park — one of the most naturally scenic school settings in Singapore. ISS offers the full IB Continuum from PYP through IB Diploma and has earned a reputation for a particularly strong arts and creative programme alongside academic rigour. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 22,577 for Kindergarten to SGD 38,647 for Grades 9-12, making it a mid-range option compared to UWCSEA or SAS. Well-suited for families seeking an arts-integrated, smaller-community school environment.

rows.title: EtonHouse International School (Orchard)
rows.summary: IB-authorised school on Tanglin Road; inquiry-based bilingual curriculum, preschool to A-Levels.
rows.body: EtonHouse International School Orchard is centrally located at 10 Tanglin Road, opposite The St. Regis Singapore, along Orchard Road. With 14 campuses across Singapore, EtonHouse is one of the island's most widespread international school networks. The Orchard campus serves as a flagship offering the full PYP through to International A-Levels. The curriculum is inquiry-based and Reggio Emilia-inspired in the early years, with a strong bilingual English-Mandarin programme. Annual tuition at the Orchard campus is approximately SGD 36,142 (primary/secondary), with additional capital levy and enrolment fees bringing first-year costs to approximately SGD 40,066. Strong university and careers guidance programme and the bespoke 'EtonCore' character-building programme.

rows.title: Stamford American International School (SAIS)
rows.summary: Full IB Continuum American school; Woodleigh campus, ages 2 months to Grade 12.
rows.body: Stamford American International School (SAIS) is an IB World School offering the complete International Baccalaureate Continuum (PYP, MYP, DP, CP) from infant care through Grade 12. The main Woodleigh Campus is at 1 Woodleigh Lane (off Upper Serangoon Road), Singapore 357684, with an Early Learning Village at 3 Chuan Lane. SAIS serves students from 2 months (infant care) through to Grade 12. The school combines American educational values with the rigour of the IB programme and has state-of-the-art facilities. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 30,820 (Grade 1) to SGD 52,980 (Grade 12), with first-year new student fees adding approximately SGD 8,000. Strong sports, arts, and extracurricular programmes.

rows.title: Chatsworth International School
rows.summary: Mid-size IB school with Orchard and East campuses; personalised education, ages 3-18.
rows.body: Chatsworth International School is a dedicated IB World School offering all three core IB programmes (PYP, MYP, IBDP) at its Orchard campus (72 Bukit Tinggi Road, approximately 10 minutes from the city centre) and East campus. Chatsworth is known for providing personalised, student-centred education in a smaller school community setting — a key differentiator from larger international schools. The school accommodates students aged 3 to 18 and has earned recognition for its IB curriculum delivery, including a Gold IB Curriculum Award. Annual tuition ranges from approximately SGD 33,382 to SGD 44,340 depending on year group. Chatsworth has offered a 100% IB Diploma scholarship for exceptional students, and is positioned as a strong mid-tier international school.

rows.title: 1er-2e arrondissement (Louvre / Bourse / Sentier)
rows.summary: Historic commercial core; prestigious address, top transit, tech-startup scene in Sentier.
rows.body: The 1st and 2nd arrondissements sit at the geographic and symbolic heart of Paris. The 1st (Louvre / Les Halles) houses the Musée du Louvre, the Palais-Royal, and the Forum des Halles shopping complex. The 2nd (Bourse / Sentier) is Paris's historic garment district reinvented as a tech-startup hub — often dubbed 'Silicon Sentier'. Both arrondissements are served by numerous Métro lines (Châtelet-Les Halles is Europe's largest underground station) making commutes effortless. Rents are among the highest in Paris, with furnished 1-bedroom apartments at €1,600–1,800/month. Limited greenspace and high tourist density are trade-offs. Best suited to young professionals, executives on short assignments, or those who want Paris at their doorstep.

rows.title: Le Marais (3e-4e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Historic central Paris; trendy, international, excellent transit.
rows.body: Le Marais covers the 3rd and 4th arrondissements of Paris. Historically a Jewish quarter and now one of the most fashionable areas, known for galleries, designer boutiques, and diverse restaurants. Popular with young professionals and international workers, especially in tech and creative industries. Excellent Métro connections (Hôtel de Ville, Rambuteau, Arts et Métiers, Saint-Paul). Rents are high but just below the 6th/7th arrondissements — furnished 1-bedrooms average €1,520–1,800/month. The 4th includes the Île Saint-Louis, one of Paris's most exclusive addresses. Limited parking — a car-free lifestyle is well-supported. The neighbourhood attracts a large LGBTQ+ community and is home to many international creatives.

rows.title: Latin Quarter & Saint-Germain-des-Prés (5e-6e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Academic and literary prestige; classic Paris atmosphere, high-income residents.
rows.body: The 5th (Latin Quarter) is home to the Sorbonne, the Panthéon, and a dense concentration of universities, making it ideal for academics and researchers. The 6th (Saint-Germain-des-Prés) is the quintessential intellectual and literary Paris — Café de Flore, historic publishing houses, high-end boutiques. Both arrondissements attract diplomats, senior academics, and high-income expat households. The 6th is one of Paris's most expensive at €40–46/m², putting a furnished 1-bedroom at €1,600–1,840/month. Very good transit (Odéon, Cluny-La Sorbonne, Saint-Michel). The area is walkable, architecturally stunning, and has a large population of English-speaking expatriates. Schools and services are excellent.

rows.title: Invalides & Eiffel Tower (7e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Embassy row; prestigious, quiet, very expensive, ideal for diplomat families.
rows.body: The 7th arrondissement is the address of choice for embassies, government ministries, and the French political establishment. It contains the Eiffel Tower, Invalides, the Musée d'Orsay, and the Rodin Museum. Exceptionally quiet and safe, with wide Haussmannian boulevards and refined neighbourhood life. Popular with diplomatic families and very senior corporate relocatees. Furnished rents at €38–43/m², with a typical 2-bedroom at €2,500–4,000/month. Served by Métro lines 8, 10, 13 and the RER C. École Jeannine Manuel (bilingual school) is located at the border of the 7th/15th. Limited nightlife but outstanding quality of life, proximity to UNESCO and international organisations.

rows.title: Champs-Élysées & Madeleine (8e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Corporate HQ district; luxury retail, iconic landmarks, premium rents.
rows.body: The 8th arrondissement is the financial and luxury commercial heart of Paris. The Avenue des Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, Élysée Palace, and the Grand Palais all sit here. It hosts the Paris HQs of many multinationals and luxury conglomerates (LVMH, L'Oréal, Total). Primarily a corporate relocation destination for executives. Furnished rents at €36–41/m², with 2-bedrooms typically €2,000–3,500/month. Excellent transit (Charles de Gaulle-Étoile, Champs-Élysées-Clémenceau, Miromesnil). The neighbourhood skews professional rather than family-oriented, though good private schools are accessible. International feel with many English-speaking businesses and services.

rows.title: Grands Boulevards & Canal Saint-Martin (9e-10e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Creative and dynamic; food scene, canal-side life, mid-range rents.
rows.body: The 9th (Opéra / South Pigalle, known as SoPi) and 10th (Canal Saint-Martin / Gare du Nord / Gare de l'Est) arrondissements represent Paris's creative-professional heartland. The 9th hosts the Paris Opéra (Garnier), a buzzing restaurant scene around Rue des Martyrs, and a dense population of young international professionals. The 10th is known for the scenic Canal Saint-Martin — iron footbridges, canal-side cafés, and independent boutiques — and is a popular landing zone for digital nomads and creatives. Furnished rents at €33–38/m², with a 2-bedroom at €1,600–2,500/month. Excellent transit including Eurostar connections at Gare du Nord. Diverse, lively, genuinely international feel.

rows.title: Bastille & Nation (11e-12e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Diverse, lively, good value; emerging family area with strong transit links.
rows.body: The 11th (Bastille / Oberkampf / République) is one of Paris's most energetic neighbourhoods, with a dense bar and restaurant scene, artisan workshops, and a young, diverse population. It has a strong expat presence among mid-career professionals. The 12th (Bercy / Nation) is quieter and more family-oriented, with the large Bois de Vincennes nearby, the Bercy entertainment complex, and good schools. Both arrondissements offer good value relative to central Paris, with furnished 2-bedrooms at €1,700–2,800/month. Strong Métro coverage (lines 1, 5, 8, 9). Paris Gare de Lyon (TGV to Lyon, Marseille, Geneva) is in the 12th, convenient for international travel.

rows.title: Butte-aux-Cailles & Chinatown (13e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Residential, diverse, more affordable; good for long-term renters and families.
rows.body: The 13th arrondissement is one of Paris's most underrated neighbourhoods. The Butte-aux-Cailles quarter retains a village-like character with independent cafés and street art. The Chinatown area around Avenue de Choisy is the largest Asian neighbourhood in Paris, with excellent pan-Asian restaurants and grocers. The Bibliothèque François Mitterrand (BnF) has anchored a major urban regeneration. Rents are among the more affordable in Paris at €28–33/m², with a 2-bedroom at €1,500–2,200/month. Good Métro access (lines 5, 6, 7). Popular with long-term expat residents who want spacious apartments at lower cost. University Paris Diderot and Paris Sorbonne Nouvelle are located here.

rows.title: Montparnasse (14e-15e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Residential and family-friendly; well-served by schools, good transport, balanced lifestyle.
rows.body: The 14th (Montparnasse / Denfert-Rochereau / Alésia) and 15th (Vaugirard / Beaugrenelle) arrondissements are the backbone of family-expat Paris. The 14th is home to the Montparnasse Tower, Roland Garros stadium (nearby), and a solid residential fabric with markets and parks. The 15th is Paris's most populous arrondissement and exceptionally liveable — excellent schools (including the prestigious École Jeannine Manuel), well-stocked markets, and the Seine riverbank. Rents at €30–36/m², with 2-bedrooms at €1,700–2,800/month furnished. Strong Métro coverage (lines 4, 6, 12, 13). ICS Paris (IB school) and Bilingual International School of Paris are both located in the 15th. Highly recommended for families on multi-year assignments.

rows.title: Passy & Trocadéro (16e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Wealthy residential enclave; quiet, family-friendly, largest expat concentration in Paris.
rows.body: The 16th arrondissement is the traditional home of wealthy Parisian families, diplomats, and expatriates. It stretches from the Trocadéro esplanade (facing the Eiffel Tower) to the Bois de Boulogne. Passy is its most populated village-like quarter, with independent shops and good schools. The International School of Paris (ISP) is located here, as is the Canadian Bilingual School. Very safe, quiet, and green — ideal for families with children. Furnished rents at €36–44/m², with 2-bedrooms at €2,200–4,000/month. Well-connected by Métro (lines 9, 10) and RER C. A significant American, British, and Northern European expat community is well-established here. Note: less nightlife and younger-professional energy than other arrondissements.

rows.title: 17e arrondissement (Batignolles / Monceau)
rows.summary: Diverse residential district; good transit, mid-range, growing expat presence.
rows.body: The 17th arrondissement is one of Paris's largest and most varied. The southern part (Monceau, Plaine de Wagram) is affluent and quiet, bordering the chic 8th. The northern part (Batignolles, Épinettes) is more bohemian and diverse, with a village-like atmosphere around Square des Batignolles park. The area has seen significant investment and is popular with young families priced out of the 8th and 16th. The EIB Monceau middle school has a campus here. Rents range from €32–42/m² depending on sub-quarter, with 2-bedrooms at €1,800–3,200/month furnished. Good Métro access (lines 2, 3, 13) and proximity to La Défense business district. A growing younger expat community values the balance of price, transit, and neighbourhood feel.

rows.title: Montmartre (18e arrondissement)
rows.summary: Artistic hilltop village; touristy near Sacré-Coeur, quieter in upper reaches.
rows.body: The 18th arrondissement is defined by the hill of Montmartre — the Sacré-Cœur basilica, Place du Tertre, and the winding streets beloved by artists for centuries. There is a sharp distinction between lower Montmartre (around Pigalle/Blanche — lively, touristy, higher rents) and upper Montmartre (Lamarck-Caulaincourt — quiet, genuinely village-like, steep streets). Rents are among the more affordable in Paris at €28–35/m², with 2-bedrooms at €1,500–2,500/month. Métro lines 2, 4, 12 provide good connectivity. Popular with creative professionals, artists, and expats seeking character over convenience. Some parts of the southern 18th (Barbès, Goutte d'Or) are rougher and require local knowledge. Northern upper Montmartre is one of Paris's hidden gems for quality of life.

rows.title: Neuilly-sur-Seine
rows.summary: Premier expat suburb; ultra-safe, excellent schools, adjacent to Bois de Boulogne.
rows.body: Neuilly-sur-Seine sits immediately west of the 16th arrondissement and the Bois de Boulogne, and is arguably the most popular suburb with expatriate families in the Paris region. It offers the feel of central Paris with more space, greenery, and exceptional safety. Home to Marymount International School Paris (72 Boulevard de la Saussaye). The suburb has excellent Métro access via line 1 (Les Sablons, Pont de Neuilly) with a direct ride to La Défense and Châtelet. Rents are high: studio €1,000–1,900/month, 2-bedroom €2,000–4,500/month furnished. Local schools, pharmacies, medical services, and international supermarkets all excellent. A strong community of American, British, and Northern European expat families is established here. Close to American Chamber of Commerce Paris and many multinational offices.

rows.title: Boulogne-Billancourt
rows.summary: Media and tech suburb; family-friendly, slightly cheaper than central Paris, great amenities.
rows.body: Boulogne-Billancourt is the most populous suburb of France and sits directly south-west of the 16th arrondissement, bordering the Bois de Boulogne. It hosts major media companies (TF1, M6, Dassault Systèmes) and has a strong tech and creative professional community. Very family-friendly, with excellent public and private schools, numerous parks, and the large Parc de Saint-Cloud nearby. Furnished rents at €1,300–2,800/month for a 2-bedroom — notably more affordable than equivalent space in the 16th. Métro line 9 and 10, plus the tram T2, give good access to central Paris (30 minutes to city centre). The waterfront around the Île Seguin (future music city development) is regenerating quickly. Popular destination for FR-DE corridor relocatees working in tech or automotive industries.

rows.title: Saint-Cloud & Versailles Corridor
rows.summary: Green, prestige suburb with international school cluster; popular with American and German expats.
rows.body: Saint-Cloud is a green, hilly suburb west of Boulogne-Billancourt, best known internationally as home to the American School of Paris (41 Rue Pasteur) and the German School Paris (18 Rue Pasteur) — both on the same street. The larger Versailles corridor (including Vélizy-Villacoublay, Jouy-en-Josas) is home to major multinationals (Renault, Thales, Safran). Saint-Cloud itself is quiet and affluent, with the spectacular Parc de Saint-Cloud. Commute to central Paris: 25–35 minutes by Transilien L-line or bus. Rents are slightly below Neuilly but above central arrondissements for comparable space: 2-bedrooms at €1,800–3,500/month. Versailles itself (30 km from Paris) offers significantly more space and good RER C access. Very popular with American, German, and Dutch corporate relocatees specifically because of the school cluster.

rows.title: American School of Paris (ASP)
rows.summary: Leading IB and American diploma school for English-speaking families in Saint-Cloud.
rows.body: Founded in 1946, the American School of Paris is one of the most established international schools in the Paris region. Located at 41 Rue Pasteur, 92210 Saint-Cloud, on a private 10.5-acre (40,000 m²) campus 25 minutes west of central Paris. Offers the American High School Diploma and full IB continuum: IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP), and Diploma Programme (DP). Ages 3–18. Approximately 900 students from 55+ nationalities. Strong athletics, arts, and STEM programmes. Annual tuition for 2026/2027: €25,000–€40,950 depending on grade level. One-time new-student registration fee: €12,200. Application fee: €1,450. Particularly popular with American corporate relocatees (FR-US corridor) and families on international assignment. The school has its own shuttle bus network across the Paris region.

rows.title: International School of Paris (ISP)
rows.summary: Paris's only full IB continuum school in the city; located in the 16th arrondissement.
rows.body: The International School of Paris (ISP) holds the distinction of being the first school in France to offer all three main IB programmes: PYP, MYP, and DP. Located across three campuses in the 16th arrondissement (primary at 96 bis Rue du Ranelagh, secondary at 6 Rue Beethoven). Ages 3–18. Approximately 900 students from 70+ nationalities. 100% English instruction. Annual tuition for 2026/2027: Nursery/Pre-K €25,500; Kindergarten €31,100; Grades 1–5 €31,400; Grades 6–9 €36,500; Grades 10–12 €39,000. One-time entry fee for new students: €10,000. Application fee: €1,000. Well-regarded academic programme with strong university placement record. The 16th arrondissement location is ideal for families already living in the area or in Neuilly-sur-Seine. Excellent public transport access via Métro 9 (Ranelagh, La Muette).

rows.title: Marymount International School Paris
rows.summary: Catholic American-tradition international school in Neuilly-sur-Seine; ages 2–14.
rows.body: Marymount International School Paris is located at 72 Boulevard de la Saussaye, 92200 Neuilly-sur-Seine — coordinates 48°53′32.5″N 2°16′10.2″E. Founded by the Religious of the Sacred Heart of Mary, it follows American and international curriculum traditions in a Catholic ethos (welcoming to all faiths). Ages 2–14 (Nursery through Grade 8 / age 14). Approximately 330 students from 35+ nationalities. Instruction in both French and English. Annual tuition for 2026/2027: €23,000–€38,000 depending on grade. One-time capital assessment fee for new students: €12,400. Application fee: €1,400. Particularly popular with American, British, Irish, and Canadian expat families. The Neuilly location is exceptionally convenient — walkable from Métro line 1 (Les Sablons). Offers strong pastoral care and a close-knit community. Note: does not offer secondary (high school) education; families typically transition to ASP or ISP for Grade 9+.

rows.title: The British School of Paris
rows.summary: British curriculum school (GCSEs and A Levels) in Croissy-sur-Seine, west of Paris.
rows.body: The British School of Paris is located at 2 Rue Hans List, 78290 Croissy-sur-Seine — approximately 25 km west of central Paris in the Yvelines department. Ages 3–18. Approximately 600 students. Offers a British curriculum throughout: Key Stages 1–4, GCSEs, and A Levels. 100% English-language instruction. Annual tuition for 2025/2026: Junior School (Nursery/Reception) approximately €20,684–€27,027; Senior School (Years 7–13) approximately €29,000–€34,065. One-time development fund contribution for new students: €8,000. Registration fee: €1,500. The school is popular with British corporate relocatees and international families seeking a British educational pathway. Located in a leafy suburban setting with its own campus grounds. Accessible by RER A (Saint-Germain-en-Laye line) and school bus. The school serves the broader western Paris corridor including Saint-Germain-en-Laye and Versailles commuter belt.

rows.title: Lycée International de Saint-Germain-en-Laye (French + International Sections)
rows.summary: Prestigious French public school with international sections including American, British, and 13 others.
rows.body: The Lycée International de Saint-Germain-en-Laye (LISG), located at 2 bis Rue du Fer à Cheval, 78100 Saint-Germain-en-Laye, is one of France's most prestigious public schools. It operates a unique model: students follow the French national curriculum and Baccalaureate alongside one of 15 international sections (American, British, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Italian, Swedish, Danish, Polish, Chinese, Arabic, Japanese, Russian, and Korean). Ages 4–18. The American Section (americansection.org) charges approximately €5,000–€6,610/year for the international section fees (the French public school component is free). The British Section charges approximately €3,746–€9,090/year. New student registration fee: €2,000. A 40-minute RER A journey west of central Paris. Highly competitive admission for international sections. The Baccalauréat Français International (BFI) awarded here is recognised globally. Popular with families seeking genuine bilingual education at moderate cost.
rows.price_range_text: €3,746-9,090/year (international section fees; French curriculum component is free public school)

rows.title: École Jeannine Manuel (EJM)
rows.summary: Top-ranked bilingual French-English school in the 15th arrondissement; IB and French Baccalaureate.
rows.body: École Jeannine Manuel (EJM) is consistently ranked as one of France's best private schools and one of the top bilingual schools in the world (ranked in the top 5 globally by The Times). Located at 70 Rue du Théâtre, 75015 Paris (15th arrondissement, near the 7th border). Ages 4–18 (Pre-K through 12th grade / Terminale). Approximately 2,800 students from 80+ nationalities. Curriculum is a 50/50 French-English bilingual programme following the French national curriculum, French Baccalaureate, and IB Diploma Programme. Annual tuition for 2026/2027: €9,935–€31,565 depending on level (Primary lower range, Lycée upper range). Application fee: €350. Very competitive admission with long waiting lists — families are advised to apply 2+ years in advance. IB Diploma results consistently above the global average. Strong university placement to Sciences Po, Grandes Écoles, Oxbridge, and Ivy League. Ideal for families planning a long stay in France or seeking genuine bilingual education for their children.

rows.title: Internationale Deutsche Schule Paris (iDSP)
rows.summary: German international school in Saint-Cloud; German Abitur and bilingual French-German education.
rows.body: The Internationale Deutsche Schule Paris (iDSP) is located at 18 Rue Pasteur, 92210 Saint-Cloud — coordinates 48°50′32″N 2°12′13″E — on the same street as the American School of Paris. Ages 3–18. Approximately 360 students. Offers the German school curriculum leading to the German Abitur and the Option Internationale du Baccalauréat (OIB). Instruction primarily in German, with French as a strong second language and English also taught. Annual tuition fees: approximately €10,684–€13,054/year — notably more affordable than most international schools in Paris, as the school is subsidised by the German government (KMK-approved). A key school for the FR-DE corridor: families relocating between Germany and France (Deutsche Telekom, Siemens, BMW, Volkswagen, BASF employees) frequently choose this school. Admission is possible throughout the year. Smaller school community provides strong pastoral support.

rows.title: ICS Paris (International Community School)
rows.summary: IB school in the 15th arrondissement; mid-range fees, strong pastoral care.
rows.body: ICS Paris (International Community School) is located in the 15th arrondissement and offers the full IB continuum from ages 3 to 18. It is noted for its welcoming, inclusive community and strong pastoral support — making it a good fit for families making their first international assignment. Instruction is primarily English (75%) with French (25%). Annual tuition for 2026/2027: €20,994–€32,976 depending on grade. Additional school development fund: €3,750 for new students. Application fee: €750. Enrolment fee: €3,000. The school has a diverse student body with over 60 nationalities represented. Located near the Parc André Citroën and well-served by Métro line 10 and tram T3a. Slightly more affordable than ISP while still offering the full IB programme. Popular with families from Scandinavian countries and the United States.

rows.title: École Active Bilingue Jeannine Manuel — EIB Schools Network
rows.summary: Network of bilingual French-English schools across multiple Paris arrondissements; affordable entry point.
rows.body: The École Active Bilingue Jeannine Manuel (EABJM) network (not to be confused with the main École Jeannine Manuel at 70 Rue du Théâtre) operates multiple campuses in central and western Paris. Key campuses include EIB Grenelle (7th arrondissement, ages 3–11), EIB Monceau Primary and Middle School (8th and 17th arrondissements, ages 3–15), and EIB Lamartine (16th arrondissement, ages 3–10). Curriculum is primarily French (75% French, 25% English at primary level), following the French national curriculum with an enhanced English-language programme. Annual tuition fees: EIB Grenelle €16,575–€17,910; EIB Monceau Primary €8,820; EIB Monceau Middle €10,200–€11,250. Application fee: €300 across all campuses. Registration fee: €1,000–€1,800 depending on campus. These schools offer a more affordable entry point into bilingual education for families planning medium-to-long stays in France, particularly those whose children will need to integrate into the French education system. Good gateway into Lycée Français pathway.
rows.price_range_text: €8,820-17,910/year tuition depending on campus and grade (2026/27)

rows.title: Upper East Side, Manhattan
rows.summary: Classic Manhattan neighbourhood; museums, international schools, corporate executives, diplomats near the UN.
rows.body: The Upper East Side (UES) is one of New York's most prestigious residential neighbourhoods. Popular with corporate expats, diplomats, and families due to proximity to the United Nations, Central Park, and several international schools. Carnegie Hill (86th–96th Street) is particularly sought after for families. Rental prices are premium. Excellent transit: 4/5/6 train, Q train, M15 bus. English-speaking services throughout. Quieter and more residential than Midtown. The Lycée Français de New York is located on East 75th Street. Museum Mile (Fifth Avenue) provides world-class cultural access.

rows.title: Upper West Side, Manhattan
rows.summary: Academic and arts-oriented neighbourhood near Columbia University; family-friendly, brownstones, Lincoln Center.
rows.body: The Upper West Side (UWS) stretches from 59th Street to 110th Street between Central Park and the Hudson River. It is home to Columbia University, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, the American Museum of Natural History, and Riverside Park. Popular with academics, media professionals, and international families. The Dwight School (IB, preschool–grade 12) is located at 291 Central Park West. Brownstones and pre-war apartment buildings dominate the housing stock. Transit: 1/2/3, B/C trains. Excellent public schools and private options. A culturally vibrant and intellectually active neighbourhood.

rows.title: Midtown East, Manhattan
rows.summary: Corporate hub adjacent to the United Nations; excellent transit, luxury residences, highly convenient for diplomats.
rows.body: Midtown East covers roughly 34th to 59th Streets east of Fifth Avenue, encompassing the Grand Central Terminal area, the United Nations Secretariat campus (First Avenue & 42nd–48th Streets), and Turtle Bay. It is the natural home for UN staff, corporate executives, and senior expats seeking maximum convenience. High-rise luxury rentals dominate. Transit: 4/5/6, E/M, S trains, multiple bus lines, easy airport access via Queens Midtown Tunnel. The neighbourhood is relatively quiet for Midtown. Nearby amenities include Bryant Park, Tudor City green spaces, and a dense array of restaurants and services.

rows.title: Murray Hill / Kips Bay, Manhattan
rows.summary: Mid-range Manhattan residential area; young professionals and families, good transit, slightly calmer pace.
rows.body: Murray Hill (34th–40th Streets, Third Avenue to the East River) and adjacent Kips Bay (27th–34th Streets) offer a more affordable entry point to Manhattan living. Popular with young expat professionals and smaller families. The British International School of New York (BISNY) is located at Waterside Plaza (20 Waterside Plaza) at the Kips Bay waterfront. Neighbourhood features include proximity to Grand Central, the Morgan Library, and Bellevue Hospital. Transit: 6 train, multiple crosstown buses. Predominantly mid-rise apartment buildings with modern amenities. Good dining along Lexington and Third Avenues.

rows.title: Battery Park City / Financial District, Manhattan
rows.summary: Modern waterfront neighbourhood; corporate families, new residential towers, Hudson River access.
rows.body: Battery Park City is a planned community on the Hudson River waterfront in lower Manhattan, filled with modern high-rise residential towers, parks, and the Esplanade. Adjacent to the Financial District (FiDi), it appeals to corporate expat families working in finance, law, or tech. The area is quieter on weekends. Residents enjoy Brookfield Place (upscale shopping/dining), the Hudson River Park, and proximity to Wall Street. Excellent schools in the area include Avenues The World School (Chelsea, nearby). Transit: 1/2/3/4/5, E, R, W, J/Z trains, plus the free BPC loop bus. Ferry service to New Jersey and Brooklyn available.
rows.district: Manhattan — Battery Park City / Financial District

rows.title: Hoboken / Jersey City, New Jersey
rows.summary: Affordable alternative to Manhattan with excellent PATH train access; popular with expat families and young professionals.
rows.body: Hoboken and Jersey City sit directly across the Hudson River from Manhattan and offer significantly lower rents while maintaining easy commute access via the PATH train (15–25 minutes to Midtown or Downtown). Hoboken has a small-town feel with waterfront parks, restaurants, and a thriving expat community. Jersey City (particularly the Newport and Grove Street areas) is rapidly developing with luxury high-rises. Both cities have international communities and growing family amenities. Key considerations: PATH trains run 24/7; NJ Transit buses also available. School options include local public schools and private options in the region. Hudson River waterfront provides scenic running and cycling paths.

rows.title: Park Slope / Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn
rows.summary: Quintessential family-friendly Brooklyn neighbourhood; brownstones, Prospect Park, strong school culture.
rows.body: Park Slope and Carroll Gardens are among Brooklyn's most desirable family neighbourhoods, known for beautiful brownstones, tree-lined streets, excellent independent restaurants and cafés, and proximity to Prospect Park. Park Slope has a strong community culture with active parents' associations and excellent public school zoning. Carroll Gardens is home to the International School of Brooklyn (ISB), a French-English and Spanish-English bilingual IB school (age 3 to grade 8). The area has a strong expat community from France, Italy, and the UK. Transit: F/G trains (Carroll Gardens), 2/3, B/Q trains (Park Slope). Shopping along Seventh Avenue and Atlantic Avenue.

rows.title: DUMBO / Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn
rows.summary: Premium Brooklyn waterfront neighbourhood; Manhattan Bridge views, cobblestone streets, tech and creative professionals.
rows.body: DUMBO (Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass) and adjacent Brooklyn Heights offer some of the most dramatic views of the Manhattan skyline and Brooklyn Bridge. Brooklyn Heights is one of the oldest and most architecturally preserved neighbourhoods in New York, with Federal and Victorian-era brownstones and the famous Brooklyn Heights Promenade. DUMBO has transformed into a tech and creative hub with galleries, boutiques, and upscale restaurants. Both areas attract affluent expat professionals. Transit: A/C, F, 2/3 trains; easy Brooklyn Bridge Park access. Proximity to Manhattan via multiple bridges and the East River Ferry.

rows.title: Astoria / Long Island City, Queens
rows.summary: Diverse, culturally rich Queens neighbourhood with strong transit links; popular mid-range option for expats.
rows.body: Astoria has long been one of New York's most diverse neighbourhoods, with large Greek, Middle Eastern, Egyptian, and Brazilian communities, among many others. It offers a vibrant restaurant scene, excellent access to Manhattan (N/W train, 20 minutes to Midtown), and mid-range rents. Long Island City (LIC), its southern neighbour, has become a tech and creative hub with luxury high-rises offering stunning Manhattan skyline views. Both areas appeal to younger expat professionals and families seeking space and value. Astoria Park provides excellent outdoor space along the East River. Transit: N/W trains (Astoria), E/M/7/G trains (LIC).

rows.title: Riverdale, Bronx
rows.summary: Suburban enclave within NYC; leafy, quiet, several international and bilingual schools nearby, popular with families.
rows.body: Riverdale is the northwesternmost neighbourhood of the Bronx, bordering Westchester County, and has a distinctly suburban character unusual within New York City. Large apartment buildings and private houses sit on hilly terrain above the Hudson River, with Van Cortlandt Park and Wave Hill botanical garden nearby. The neighbourhood has a significant Jewish, Irish-American, and international community. Several independent and bilingual schools serve the area, and the Riverdale Country School is a well-regarded independent day school. Easy Westchester commute access. Transit: 1 train (Henry Hudson Pkwy area), express buses to Midtown. Quieter and more spacious than most NYC neighbourhoods.

rows.title: Williamsburg, Brooklyn
rows.summary: Creative and tech-forward neighbourhood; popular with young expats, excellent transit, vibrant dining and arts scene.
rows.body: Williamsburg has evolved from an artistic enclave to one of Brooklyn's most sought-after addresses, attracting tech workers, creative professionals, and international young expats from Europe, Israel, and Latin America. The neighbourhood features excellent restaurants and bars along Bedford Avenue, waterfront parks with Manhattan skyline views, weekend markets, and a thriving cultural scene. Families are increasingly present, particularly in South Williamsburg and along the waterfront. Transit: L train (direct to Manhattan's 14th Street corridor), J/M/Z trains. The L train runs frequently and is generally reliable. South Williamsburg has a large Hasidic Jewish community that creates a distinct character.

rows.title: Forest Hills, Queens
rows.summary: Quiet, suburban-feel Queens neighbourhood; family-friendly, multiple language communities, good transit.
rows.body: Forest Hills is a residential Queens neighbourhood known for its Tudor-style garden district architecture, excellent public schools, and diverse international community with strong Russian, Korean, Greek, and South Asian populations. The USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center is nearby. Forest Hills Gardens — a planned garden community — is considered one of the most attractive residential enclaves in the borough. Relatively quiet and green, with a distinctly European café culture along Austin Street. Transit: E/F/M/R trains (approx. 25 minutes to Midtown). Good value for families seeking space and community without Manhattan prices.

rows.title: United Nations International School (UNIS)
rows.summary: IB World School for the international diplomatic community; PreK–12, multilingual, Queens campus.
rows.body: UNIS was founded in 1947 to serve the children of United Nations staff and has grown into one of New York's premier international schools. Located at 24–50 FDR Drive in Manhattan (with a satellite Queens campus at Jamaica) — the primary campus is at 24–50 FDR Drive, New York, NY 10010 (Sutton Place / Midtown East waterfront). The school offers the full IB continuum from Primary Years Programme through to the IB Diploma. Over 100 nationalities are represented in the student body. The school is affiliated with UNESCO and UNICEF. Annual tuition ranges from approximately $46,856 to $53,767 depending on grade (2024–25 figures). Ages 4–18.

rows.title: French-American School of New York (FASNY)
rows.summary: Bilingual French-English N–12 day school in Mamaroneck and Larchmont, Westchester County; French Baccalaureate and IB.
rows.body: FASNY was founded in 1980 and operates across three campuses in Westchester County: HQ and Grades 9–12 at 320 East Boston Post Road, Mamaroneck, NY 10543; Nursery–Grade 3 at 111 Larchmont Avenue, Larchmont, NY 10538; Grades 4–8 at 145 New Street, Mamaroneck. The school follows the French curriculum alongside IB preparation and admits students aged 3–18. A preferred option for French diplomatic families and French company expats, as well as families seeking genuine bilingual French-English education. Annual tuition ranges from approximately $37,950 (lower grades) to $46,825 (upper grades). Commutable from Upper Manhattan via Metro-North (30–40 minutes from Grand Central). Ages 3–18.

rows.title: Lycée Français de New York
rows.summary: Prestigious French-curriculum international school in Manhattan's Upper East Side; ages 3–18, bilingual, over 1,200 students.
rows.body: The Lycée Français de New York (LFNY) is located at 505 East 75th Street, New York, NY 10021 (Upper East Side). Founded in 1935, it is one of the largest French bilingual schools outside France and follows the French Ministry of Education curriculum alongside the IB Diploma. Over 1,200 students from 60+ countries attend. The school prepares students for both the French Baccalaureate and the IB Diploma Programme. Annual tuition is approximately $49,925–$51,925 for all grades (Nursery-3 through Grade 12). Ages 3–18. It is a French government-recognised institution managed under AEFE (Agence pour l'Enseignement Français à l'Étranger).

rows.title: Dwight School New York
rows.summary: IB World School on the Upper West Side; pioneer of the IB programme, preschool–grade 12, established 1872.
rows.body: Dwight School is located at 291 Central Park West, New York, NY 10024 (Upper West Side). Founded in 1872, it is one of the oldest private schools in New York and a pioneer of the International Baccalaureate — it was among the first US schools to offer the full IB continuum from Preschool-2s through Grade 12. The school admits students from age 2 through 18. Annual tuition ranges from approximately $18,900 (nursery programmes) to $69,950 (upper school, grades 1–12). The school operates on a global network of affiliated Dwight campuses worldwide, making it popular with internationally mobile families. Dwight offers extensive arts, athletics, and STEAM programmes alongside IB.
rows.district: Manhattan — Upper West Side (Central Park West)

rows.title: Avenues: The World School
